newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba officials rules out another German rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Buba officials rules out another German rate cut.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Wednesday that he would rule out chances for another key interest rate cut as such a move could be interpreted as eroding trust in the central bank's policies.

"Another rate cut could backfire as it could erode the trust in the Bundesbank's stability-oriented policies," Jochimsen, also the president of the state central bank in North Rhine-Westphalia, said in a text prepared for delivery at the inauguration of a building here.
The text was made available beforehand.
Jochimsen said that Germany's problems could not be solved through lower interest rates alone and urged that clear and dependable fiscal policies were necessary.
Nervousness that the Bundesbank might however be forced to end its five year easing cycle and raise rates has increased especially after several other countries hiked rates.
The U.K. on Tuesday markets lifted base rates to 6.25 percent just weeks after the U.S. fired a similar warning shot at revived inflationary pressures in late March.
The Bundesbank last raised interest rates in the summer of 1992. It last cut its key discount and Lombard rates to 2.50 and 4.50 respectively in April 1996.
The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was cut to three percent last August.
